title: The symmetric-product morphism is a morphism over the base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $n\ge1$. Write $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ and $\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with structure morphisms $q_1:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ and $q_n=\mathrm{pr}_1:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$, and let $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n=\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\cdots\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ be the $n$-fold fibre product over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product] (formed inductively, $(\mathbf P^1_S)^1=\mathbf P^1_S$, $p_1=q_1$, $(\mathbf P^1_S)^{m}=(\mathbf P^1_S)^{m-1}\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$, $p_m=p_{m-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$), with its projection $p_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to S$. Let $\sigma_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^n_S$ be the symmetric-product morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties], given by $((x_1:y_1),\dots,(x_n:y_n))\mapsto[F_0:\cdots:F_n]$ with $\prod_i(x_it+y_i)=\sum_jF_jt^j$, and constructed as the morphism $\varphi_{p_n,(\mathcal L_n,(F_0,\dots,F_n))}$ of [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] attached to the projection $p_n$, the invertible module $\mathcal L_n=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathrm{pr}_n^*\mathcal O(1)$ and its generating global sections $F_0,\dots,F_n$. Then $\sigma_n$ is a morphism over $S$: $q_n\circ\sigma_n=p_n$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4F (label lemma-reduce-to-P1), proof, last paragraph ("For every $n \geq 1$ there is a finite surjective morphism ... Applying Lemmas 0A4C, 0A4E, 0A4D one more time"): the $F_j$ are polynomials with integer coefficients, so the morphism is defined over $\mathbf Z$ and base changed to $S$; the source uses $q_n\circ\sigma_n=p_n$ implicitly when it applies Lemma 0A4C

proof.text: *The construction of $\sigma_n$.* The node that constructs $\sigma_n$ is [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties]: [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism] only gives the polynomials $F_j$ and the coordinate formula, and [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties] shows that the $F_j$ have no common zero on $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$, i.e. that the sections $F_0,\dots,F_n$ of $\mathcal L_n$ (the $F_j$ are multihomogeneous of degree one in each pair $(x_i,y_i)$, so they are global sections of $\mathcal L_n$, the $x_i,y_i$ being the sections $T_0,T_1$ of $\mathcal O(1)$ pulled back by $\mathrm{pr}_i$) generate $\mathcal L_n$, and concludes that they give $\sigma_n$. Following Stacks 0A4F, whose $F_j$ are 'polynomials with integer coefficients', the pair $(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))$ defines a morphism $\psi_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, and, as Stacks says after Definition 01NF, combined with the structure morphism $p_n$ into $S$ it gives the morphism into $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$: this is $\sigma_n=\varphi_{p_n,(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))}$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], the unique morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma_n=p_n$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n=\psi_n$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4F (label lemma-reduce-to-P1), proof, last paragraph; with literature/stacks-project/constructions.tex, Section 27.13 (Tag 01ND), Lemma 27.13.1 (Tag 01NE) and the paragraph after Definition 27.13.2 (Tag 01NF)

proof.text: *$\sigma_n$ is over $S$.* By [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] the structure morphism $q_n$ of $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ is the first projection $\mathrm{pr}_1$. Hence, by step 1 and the defining property of the morphism into a fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], $q_n\circ\sigma_n=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma_n=p_n$. (Equivalently, on functors of points: a $T$-point of $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ lying over $t:T\to S$ goes to the $T$-point $(t,\psi_n\circ-)$ of $S\times\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, which lies over the same $t$; no chart computation is needed, because the integrality of the coefficients of the $F_j$ is what lets the $\mathbf P^n$-component be taken over $\mathbf Z$ while the $S$-component is $p_n$ itself.)
